stopbang.title: STOP-Bang Risk Index for Obstructive Sleep Apnea

preface.definition:
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) [ 26 ] is the most prevalent sleep-breathing disturbance, 
                                affecting about 34% of men and 17% of women.
                                A sleep apnea episode is a cessation of breathing (apnea) or 
                                a marked reduction in airflow (hypopnea) during sleep.
                                An episode is considered clinically relevant if it lasts more than 10 seconds; 
                                episodes of apneas and hypopneas often persist for 30-60 seconds.
                                It is estimated that the average life span of someone with untreated OSA is 58 years.

acb.title: Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB)
acb.root_preface:
Many medications can induce "brain fog,"
                                an additional layer of impairment that may mask actual cognitive decline.
                                In particular, the additive effects of anticholinergic medications, 
                                known as their Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB),
                                have been well studied. [ 4-7 ] The total ACB score evaluates the degree of impairment induced by someone's
                                current medications.
                                Each medication is scored from 0 to 3, and these scores are summed.
                                The criteria for these "0 to 3" values are:

Termed a possible anticholinergic.

A definite anticholinergic.

headers: Potential alternatives offering a lower ACB Score

postface.text:
The total ACB score is 7 . This cognitive burden adds a layer of masking atop any existing
                                cognitive decline, making it difficult to determine someone's actual status.    Notes: Each definite anticholinergic,
                                of which there are currently 2 ,
                                may increase the risk of cognitive impairment
                                by 46% over 6 years. For each one-point increase in the total ACB score, 
                                a decline in someone's Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score
                                of 0.33 points over 2 years has been suggested. 
                                
                                Thus, the current anticholinergic burden may be lowering an MMSE score by 2 points.

leqembi.heading: Assessing Eligibility for Leqembi
leqembi.legend_preface:
A genetic analysis, amyloid positivity, and a brain MRI scan are required 
    to be eligible for these treatments,
    after first satisfying a number of initial criteria, shown below. [ 29 ]
preface:
Leqembi (generic name: lecanemab )
    is a prescription medication designed to treat Alzheimer's disease (AD).
    It is a monoclonal antibody that can
    reduce buildup of aggregated forms of amyloid beta, 
    which is frequently seen in the brains of those with AD.
    Leqembi
    is likely to be most effective in early stages of cognitive decline, 
    that is,
    for those diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) 
    or 
    mild Alzheimer's disease.
    It is administered via a series of monthly intravenous (IV) infusions.

fall_risk.heading: Medications That May Increase Fall Risk
preface: These existing conditions may raise the likelihood of falling: Obstructive sleep apnea ; Depression ; Lower Back Pain ; and Occasional Abdominal Pain .  In addition, five current medications are identified as fall-risk increasing drugs (FRIDs).  Their total score of 7 signifies that these medications may increase the likelihood of a fall, and further evaluation is warranted. [ 15,16 ] The STOPPFall guidelines can assist in stopping, switching, or reducing the dosage of these medications. [ 17 ] Target a total score of 5 or less.
